details.whyNow: You cannot measure what you don't understand, and you cannot design solutions to problems you haven't properly characterized. Current AI safety work focuses on aligning individual systems, but risks like gradual disempowerment emerge from how multiple agents and systems coordinate (or fail to coordinate) at scale. We need theoretical frameworks that bridge computer science, economics, political science, and complexity science to even articulate the right problems.
details.whatWereDoing: We're establishing frameworks for understanding how coordination mechanisms maintain or lose alignment with human values as systems scale. This includes developing taxonomies of agency across different scales (the "phylogeny of agents"), mapping catastrophic coordination failures (like gradual disempowerment), and identifying high-priority problems where better mechanisms could prevent existential risks. This theoretical work scopes what we'll build infrastructure to test.
details.progressAndScope: We've published foundational research on gradual disempowerment (how economic, cultural, and political systems drift from human interests), phylogeny of agents (understanding different types of agency across disciplines), and toy models of system-level safety evaluations (demonstrating multi-agent evaluation approaches). Current work includes synthesizing these insights into coherent frameworks, identifying 3-5 specific coordination challenges to focus on, and building the research community needed for subsequent phases. This phase completes when we have validated theoretical frameworks and concrete specifications for what evaluation infrastructure needs to test.
